The value names the thread: the SAME name shares one warm worker (work time-shares that one CPU), DIFFERENT names run on parallel threads. `params` is the only data that crosses and becomes the worker's context (`$x`); `ArrayBuffer`s in `params` transfer zero-copy (and detach on the sender). The node resolves to the worker's result, so collect N at once with `{ map, parallel: true, do: { thread } }`, or add the universal `then` to make the call FIRE-AND-FORGET (returns immediately; `then` runs on the main thread with `$result`). Note: a worker has no DOM/`window`/`localStorage`/WebGL, so it is for compute, `fetch`, and crypto. `thread` is a MAIN-thread node: don't nest it inside another `thread`'s `do` (it isn't available there). For parallelism use sibling threads from the main thread, e.g. `{ map, parallel: true, do: { thread } }`.

**Properties:**
- `params`: Object passed to the thread: the ONLY data that crosses, and the worker's context (its keys become `$key`). `ArrayBuffer` values transfer zero-copy (detaching the source). Must be structured-cloneable (no DOM nodes, functions, class instances).
- `do`: Steps to run on the thread, resolved against `params` as context.
- `idle`: Milliseconds to keep the thread warm after its last step before reaping it (default 10000). `0` reaps immediately; a large value keeps a long-lived thread.

**Returns:** The worker's result (a Promise the resolver awaits). Errors run the `catch` array with `$error` bound, like any node.

app-path.markdownDescription: Resolve a well-known app path by name (e.g. `userData`, `home`, `documents`) — the place to keep save games.

app-version.markdownDescription: The version from the app's package.json, for an About box or a crash report.

app-locale.markdownDescription: The user's current locale, e.g. `en-GB`. Available only after the app is ready.

app-relaunch.markdownDescription: Restart the app: queues a fresh instance and quits this one. Use after a settings change that only applies at startup.

app-on.markdownDescription:
Run steps when an application event fires.
Listeners add rather than replace, so this does not disturb the runner's own lifecycle handling — an `activate` handler runs alongside the default window restore, it does not suppress it.

**Properties:**
- `do` *(required)*: Steps run in the main process when the event fires. An array runs as a sequence; a single expression is run on its own.

dialog-open.markdownDescription:
Show a native open dialog titled with the given string. Resolves to the array of selected paths (empty if cancelled).

**Properties:**
- `properties`: What the dialog can select (e.g. openFile, openDirectory, multiSelections).
- `filters`: File-type filters that populate the dialog's format dropdown.
- `defaultPath`: Path the dialog opens at.

dialog-save.markdownDescription:
Show a native save dialog titled with the given string. Resolves to the chosen path, or an empty string if the user cancelled.

**Properties:**
- `defaultPath`: Path and filename the dialog opens with.
- `buttonLabel`: Label for the confirm button.
- `filters`: File-type filters that populate the dialog's format dropdown.

**Returns:** The path the user chose, or `""` on cancel — so `empty` distinguishes the two without a separate flag.

dialog-message.markdownDescription:
Show a native message box with the given message. Resolves to the index of the pressed button.

**Properties:**
- `buttons`: Button labels; the result is the pressed button's index.
- `type`: Icon/style of the box.
- `title`: Window title of the box.
- `detail`: Extra detail text below the message.

menu.markdownDescription:
Set the native menu from a JSON item tree. Calling it again replaces the current menu, which is how you grey out an item or toggle a checkbox — there is no separate update op.
Without `window` this is the application menu. With it, the menu attaches to that window alone (on macOS, where the menu bar belongs to the app, the focused window's menu becomes the application menu).
`do` steps run in the **main** process with `$menuLabel`, `$menuId` and `$menuChecked` bound; DOM ops inside them are forwarded to the window automatically.
The tree may be an expression instead of a literal — `{ "var": "$menu" }`, or a file. Load a file with `"data": true`, otherwise it is resolved as an expression and the `do` handlers are destroyed before they arrive.

**Properties:**
- `window`: Attach to this window instead of setting the application menu.

notify.markdownDescription:
Show a native desktop notification. The value is the title.
This is the OS notification centre, not the Web Notification API — it needs no permission prompt and no service worker, unlike the browser `sw-notify` path.

**Properties:**
- `body`: Message text below the title.
- `subtitle`: Secondary line (macOS only).
- `silent`: Suppress the notification sound.
- `icon`: Path to an image shown alongside.
- `do`: Steps run in the main process when the notification is clicked.

shell-open.markdownDescription:
Open a URL in the user's default browser, or a `mailto:` in their mail client.
Only `http`, `https` and `mailto` are allowed. Anything else is refused, because this asks the OS to launch whatever is registered for the scheme — a `file://` URL runs an executable on Windows, and a custom protocol reaches any app that claimed it.
To open a local file with its default application, use `shell-open-path`.

shell-open-path.markdownDescription:
Open a local file or folder with whatever application owns that type.
Throws if the OS could not open it, so handle that with a `catch` rather than a return value.

shell-show.markdownDescription: Reveal a file in the system file manager, selected — Explorer on Windows, Finder on macOS.

shell-trash.markdownDescription:
Move a file or folder to the Recycle Bin or Trash. Recoverable by the user, unlike deleting it.
Throws if the OS refused — a locked file, a missing path, no permission — so handle that with a `catch`.
examples: { "shell-trash": { "var": "$oldSave" }, "catch": [{ "notify": "Could not move it to the bin" }] }

shortcut.markdownDescription:
Register a **system-wide** keyboard shortcut, which fires even when the app is not focused.
For shortcuts that should only work inside your own window, use a `keydown` handler in the page's `events` map instead — those do not steal the key from every other application.
Steps run in the main process. Since a global shortcut usually fires while another app has focus, DOM ops inside them target the default window rather than the focused one.

**Properties:**
- `do`: Steps run in the main process when the shortcut fires.

**Returns:** `true` if the OS accepted the registration. `false` means another application already owns that combination.

shortcut-remove.markdownDescription: Unregister one accelerator, or every one when given `true`.

tray.markdownDescription:
Put an icon in the system tray. The value is the icon path, relative to the project root.
Calling it again updates the existing tray in place rather than adding a second one, so this doubles as the update path for the tooltip or the menu.
**A tray app outlives its windows**: closing the last window no longer quits on Windows or Linux, because minimize-to-tray is the whole point. Give the tray menu a Quit item, or the app becomes unkillable from the UI.

**Properties:**
- `tooltip`: Hover text for the tray icon.
- `items`: Right-click menu, using the same item shape as `menu`.
- `do`: Steps run in the main process when the icon is clicked.

tray-destroy.markdownDescription: Remove the tray icon. This also restores the normal quit rule, so closing the last window ends the app again.

window-open.markdownDescription:
Open a BrowserWindow showing a JSON page template over `app://` — the value is the template file from `src/` (e.g. `settings.json`, default `index.json`). A generated shell mounts it at runtime; there is no HTML file.
The window is registered under `name`, or under the template's basename (`settings.json` becomes `settings`, deduped `settings-2`). The first window opened becomes the default target for every other `window-*` op.

**Properties:**
- `name`: Register the window under this name instead of the template basename.
- `width`: Window width in pixels.
- `height`: Window height in pixels.
- `fullscreen`: Open the window fullscreen.
- `title`: Window title.
- `frame`: Set `false` for a frameless window, so the page can draw its own title bar.
- `allow`: Ops this window's page may ask the main process for. Omit for no restriction.
List ops only — a sibling travels with its op, so `["query"]` already covers `{ "query": "select", "table": "saves" }`. Nested values are checked too, so a denied op cannot hide in a sibling slot.
Your own menu, tray and shortcut handlers are unaffected — they run in main and never cross the IPC channel this limits.
- `titleBarStyle`: Native title bar treatment. `hidden` keeps the traffic lights on macOS while freeing the bar for custom chrome.

**Returns:** The name the window was registered under — pass it to `window-close` and friends.

window-close.markdownDescription: Close a window. The value names it; `true` closes the calling window, falling back to the default.

window-focus.markdownDescription: Bring a window to the front, restoring it first if minimized.

window-max.markdownDescription: Maximize a window, or unmaximize it if already maximized.

window-restore.markdownDescription: Restore a minimized or maximized window to its normal size.

window-devtools.markdownDescription: Toggle the developer tools for a window.

window-title.markdownDescription:
Set a window's title.

**Properties:**
- `window`: Name of the window to act on. Defaults to the calling window, then to the default window.

window-bounds.markdownDescription:
Move and/or resize a window. Any of `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` may be omitted to leave that axis alone.

**Properties:**
- `window`: Name of the window to act on. Defaults to the calling window, then to the default window.

window-list.markdownDescription:
List every open window with its name, id, title, state and bounds.

**Returns:** An array of `{ name, id, title, visible, minimized, maximized, focused, bounds }` objects, in the order the windows were opened.

window-run.markdownDescription:
Run steps inside a window's page, where the DOM lives.
Most of the time this is unnecessary — a DOM op written in a main-process handler is forwarded to the default window automatically. Reach for this when you need a *specific* window, since a per-op `window` sibling is impossible: DOM ops are declared by `@jexs/client`, and one package cannot add a sibling to another package's op.
Steps are sent unresolved and run in the target renderer against the page context, so they see the same state the page's own event handlers do.

**Properties:**
- `window`: Name of the window to act on. Defaults to the calling window, then to the default window.
- `params`: Values merged into the steps' scope, resolved in the main process before they cross.

**Returns:** Whatever the last step evaluates to, brought back across the bridge.

gl-init.markdownDescription:
Initializes a WebGL canvas (WebGL2 with WebGL1 fallback). Pass the canvas CSS selector as `gl-init`.
Use `width`/`height` to set logical size, `clear` for background color, `depth: true` for 3D depth test.
Pass `on-frame` steps to run every animation frame — receives `$dt` (delta seconds) and `$time` in context.

**Properties:**
- `width`: Logical canvas width in pixels.
- `height`: Logical canvas height in pixels.
- `clear`: Background clear color as `[r, g, b, a]` (default `[0,0,0,1]`).
- `depth`: Enable depth testing for 3D rendering.
- `on-frame`: Steps to run each animation frame (`$dt`, `$time` available).

gl-destroy.markdownDescription: Destroys the active WebGL instance and releases GPU resources, textures, and the entity store.

gl-hit.markdownDescription:
Hit-tests a point against all visible entities (front-to-back). Returns the topmost entity id or `null`.
Supports 2D (AABB/circle) and 3D (ray-AABB) automatically based on the current render mode.

**Properties:**
- `x`: Screen X coordinate.
- `y`: Screen Y coordinate.

gl-camera.markdownDescription:
Controls the camera. In 2D: `x`, `y`, `zoom`, `rotation`, `follow` (entity id).
Shake: `shake` (intensity), `shakeDuration`, `shakeDecay`. Trauma: `trauma` (0–1 accumulated).
In 3D: `z`, `fov`, `near`, `far`, `lookAt` ([x,y,z]), `up` ([x,y,z]).

**Properties:**
- `x`: Camera X position.
- `y`: Camera Y position.
- `zoom`: Camera zoom factor.
- `follow`: Entity ID to follow.
- `shake`: Shake intensity.

gl-texture.markdownDescription:
Loads an image from `src` and registers it as a named texture. Assign to entities via `texture: "name"`.

**Properties:**
- `src`: URL of the image to load.
- `linear`: Use LINEAR filtering instead of NEAREST (default). Set for smooth/upscaled textures and MSDF atlases.
- `hdr`: Decode `src` as a Radiance `.hdr` (RGBE) image and upload a float texture (values may exceed 1.0). Use for an equirectangular environment map referenced by a `skybox` setting.

gl-register-mesh.markdownDescription:
Uploads an imported mesh's geometry to the GPU and stores the handle on
`MeshEntry.gpu` (interleaved layout: pos3 + normal3 + uv2 = 32 bytes/vert).
Idempotent — re-uploading the same id is a no-op.

Auto-registers in the physics EntityStore if not yet present (so callers
can skip the separate `register-mesh` step). If a baseColor texture URI is
present on the material, a texture load is also kicked off.

**Properties:**
- `bounds`: AABB bounds object { min, max }.
- `positions`: Float32Array of XYZ vertex positions.
- `normals`: Float32Array of per-vertex normals (optional).
- `uvs`: Float32Array of per-vertex UVs (optional).
- `indices`: Uint16Array / Uint32Array of triangle indices (optional).
- `material`: Material URI map (optional).

gl-atlas.markdownDescription:
Loads a spritesheet and pre-computes UV rects for each frame. Pass `cols` and `rows` to define the grid.
Returns the total frame count. Use frame indices with `gl-animate` or `gl-frame`.

**Properties:**
- `src`: URL of the spritesheet image.
- `cols`: Number of columns in the grid.
- `rows`: Number of rows in the grid.

gl-animate.markdownDescription:
Starts a frame animation on an entity from an atlas. Pass `atlas`, `frames` (array of frame indices),
`fps`, and `loop`. Set `stop: true` to cancel the current animation.

**Properties:**
- `atlas`: Atlas name (registered via `gl-atlas`).
- `frames`: Array of frame indices from the atlas.
- `fps`: Frames per second for the animation.
- `loop`: Whether to loop the animation.
- `stop`: Pass `true` to stop the current animation.

gl-frame.markdownDescription:
Sets a static atlas frame on an entity (no animation). Pass entity id, `atlas`, and `frame` index.

**Properties:**
- `atlas`: Atlas name (registered via `gl-atlas`).
- `frame`: Frame index within the atlas.

gl-tilemap.markdownDescription:
Builds an efficient GPU tilemap VBO from a 2D array of atlas frame indices.
Pass `atlas`, `data` (rows of frame indices), `tileWidth`, `tileHeight`, and optional `z`.
Returns the rendered tile count.

**Properties:**
- `atlas`: Atlas name (registered via `gl-atlas`).
- `data`: 2D array of atlas frame indices (rows × columns).
- `tileWidth`: Width of each tile in pixels (default `32`).
- `tileHeight`: Height of each tile in pixels (default `32`).

gl-tilemap-set.markdownDescription:
Changes one tile of a tilemap built by `gl-tilemap` and rebuilds its VBO. Out-of-range coordinates and unknown tilemap names are a no-op.

**Properties:**
- `x` *(required)*: Column of the tile to change (0-based).
- `y` *(required)*: Row of the tile to change (0-based).
- `tile` *(required)*: Atlas frame index to write. `0` clears the tile.

gl-trail.markdownDescription:
Attaches a motion trail to an entity. The trail follows the entity's position each frame.
Pass entity id, `length` (max trail points), `width`, and `color`.

**Properties:**
- `length`: Maximum number of trail points (default `20`).
- `width`: Trail line width in pixels (default `2`).
- `color`: Trail color as `[r, g, b, a]`.

gl-trail-remove.markdownDescription: Removes the motion trail from an entity.

gl-raycast.markdownDescription:
Casts a ray from `from` in direction `dir` and returns all hit entities sorted by distance.
Pass `mask` (array of group names) to restrict which entities are tested.

**Properties:**
- `from`: Origin vector `{x, y, z?}`.
- `dir`: Direction vector `{x, y, z?}`.
- `mask`: Group names to test against (default: all groups).

gl-text.markdownDescription:
Renders text onto a canvas texture and assigns it to an entity. Creates the entity if it doesn't exist.
Pass entity id, `text`, `font` (CSS font string), `fill` (color), and position `x`, `y`, `z`.

**Properties:**
- `text`: Text content to render.
- `font`: CSS font string for the canvas path (e.g. `"24px Arial"`). Ignored when `msdf` is set.
- `fill`: CSS color string for the text fill.
- `msdf`: Name of a registered `gl-font` to render this text via the MSDF path (crisp at any scale, recolorable). When set, `font` is ignored and `size` controls the px size.
- `size` *(with `msdf`)*: Font size in px for the MSDF path. Default `32`.

gl-font.markdownDescription:
Registers an MSDF font from a pre-loaded atlas texture + parsed BMFont metrics, so `gl-text` with a matching `font` renders crisp at any scale (recolorable, one shared atlas).
Load the atlas PNG with `gl-texture` and the metrics JSON with a file/fetch node, then pass the texture name as `atlas` and the parsed JSON as `metrics`.

**Properties:**
- `atlas`: Name of a `gl-texture` holding the MSDF atlas PNG.
- `metrics`: Parsed BMFont-JSON descriptor (from a file/fetch node), or a JSON string.

gl-shader.markdownDescription:
Compiles and registers a custom GLSL shader program. Pass `name`, `vert` (vertex source), and `frag` (fragment source).
Assign to entities with `shader: "name"`. Standard uniforms (`u_transform`, `u_texture`, `u_time`, etc.) are auto-bound.

**Properties:**
- `vert`: GLSL vertex shader source.
- `frag`: GLSL fragment shader source.

gl-blur.markdownDescription: Applies a full-screen Gaussian blur post-process effect. Pass the blur radius in pixels; `0` disables it.

gl-transition.markdownDescription:
Plays a fade transition overlay. Pass `duration` in seconds (default 0.5).

**Properties:**
- `duration`: Transition duration in seconds (default `0.5`).

gl-tween.markdownDescription:
Animates numeric entity properties over time. Pass entity id, target values (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `angle`, `opacity`, `color`, etc.),
`duration` (seconds), and `easing` (e.g. `"easeOutQuad"`, `"linear"`).
The step finishes when the tween does, so a step list waits for it; add `then` to carry on without waiting and run steps once it finishes. It also finishes early when a newer tween takes over all of its properties, or the scene is destroyed.

**Properties:**
- `duration`: Animation duration in seconds (default `0.3`).
- `easing`: Easing function name.

**Returns:** `null`, once the tween finishes.

gl-ssao.markdownDescription:
Enables screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO) for 3D scenes. Pass `radius`, `bias`, and `intensity`.
Set `gl-ssao: false` to disable.

gl-particle.markdownDescription:
GPU-accelerated particle system. Pass `true` for a one-shot burst, or use operations:
- `"create"` — register a named emitter (`id`, `max`, `life`, `speed`, `continuous`, `rate`)
- `"emit"` — burst from a named emitter (`id`, `x`, `y`, `z`, `count`)
- `"destroy"` — remove a named emitter
All modes support `color`, `colorEnd`, `size`, `sizeEnd`, `life`, `speed`.

entity-init.markdownDescription:
Creates a new entity store and sets it as the active context store.
Pass `width` and `height` to define the world bounds.

**Properties:**
- `width`: World width in pixels (default `800`).
- `height`: World height in pixels (default `600`).
- `shared`: Back the store with SharedArrayBuffers so the host can step physics on a worker thread (off the main thread). Falls back to a normal store if growable SAB is unsupported. Default `false`.

entity-add.markdownDescription:
Adds an entity to the active store, under the id in `entity-add`.
The transform is `translation` / `scale` / `rotation` (there is no `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`); `angle`, `rx`, `ry` and `rotation-velocity` are shorthands that build the quaternion for you.
Set `physics: true` to simulate it and `fixed: true` for an immovable body, and `pooled: true` to reuse a pooled slot.
Any sibling not listed here is kept verbatim on the entity's `custom` metadata.

**Properties:**
- `type`: Entity shape (default `"quad"`). A shape with depth (`scale[2]` above 0) is drawn solid and flat otherwise, so a `circle` is a disc or a cylinder and a `triangle` a triangle or a cone.
`line`, `line-strip` and `points` take their geometry from `vertices`; `mesh` draws the mesh named by `mesh`, taking its scale from the mesh bounds and colliding against its BVH; `ramp` collides as a slope rather than a box; `light` and `pivot` are never drawn.
  - `light`
  - `line`
  - `line-strip`
- `group`: Collision group name (default `"default"`).
- `mask`: Collision groups this entity is tested against (default `["default"]`).
- `mesh`: Id of a mesh registered in the store. Under `entity-add: "mesh"` its bounds also become the entity's scale, so the collision AABB matches the geometry; on any other shape the mesh is render-only.
- `vertices`: Flat vertex list, for the `line`, `line-strip` and `points` types.
- `parent`: Id of a parent entity: this entity's transform becomes relative to it. Pass an empty value to detach.
- `translation`: Position `[x, y, z]` (default `[0, 0, 0]`). This is the position field; there is no `x`/`y`.
- `scale`: Size `[sx, sy, sz]` (default `[1, 1, 1]`). This is the size field; there is no `w`/`h`.
- `rotation`: Rotation quaternion `[qx, qy, qz, qw]` (default `[0, 0, 0, 1]`).
- `angle`: Z-axis rotation in degrees, converted to `rotation` for you.
- `rx`: X-axis rotation in degrees, converted to `rotation` for you.
- `ry`: Y-axis rotation in degrees, converted to `rotation` for you.
- `rotation-velocity`: Derive `rotation` from a velocity vector `[x, y, z]`, so the entity faces the way it travels.
- `vx`: Velocity along X.
- `vy`: Velocity along Y.
- `vz`: Velocity along Z.
- `ax`: Constant acceleration along X, added to gravity each step.
- `ay`: Constant acceleration along Y, added to gravity each step.
- `az`: Constant acceleration along Z, added to gravity each step.
- `mass`: Body mass (default `1`). `0` makes it infinitely heavy, so collisions never move it.
- `restitution`: Bounciness from 0 (dead stop) to 1 (no energy lost).
- `friction`: Surface friction applied on contact.
- `damping`: Per-entity velocity damping from 0 to 1, overriding the world's `damping`.
- `moveX`: Pin the X velocity each step, after gravity and damping, for driven (character-style) movement. Pass `null` to hand the axis back to the simulation.
- `moveY`: Pin the Y velocity each step, after gravity and damping, for driven (character-style) movement. Pass `null` to hand the axis back to the simulation.
- `physics`: Simulate this entity. Without it the entity is drawn but never stepped.
- `fixed`: Immovable body: it collides but is never moved by a collision.
- `visible`: Draw this entity (default `true`). Hiding one hides its children too.
- `color`: RGBA `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1 (default `[1, 1, 1, 1]`).
- `uv`: Texture sub-rect `[u, v, w, h]`, for drawing one frame out of an atlas.
- `opacity`: Opacity from 0 to 1.
- `texture`: Name of a texture loaded with `gl-texture`.
- `normalMap`: Name of a texture to light the surface with as a normal map.
- `normalScale`: How strongly `normalMap` perturbs the surface.
- `borderRadius`: Corner radius in pixels, rounding the box an entity with depth (`scale[2]` above 0) is drawn as. It replaces the shape's geometry outright, so it is for a quad.
- `shader`: Name of a custom shader registered with `gl-shader`.
- `blend`: Blend mode (default `"normal"`).
- `emissive`: Draw at full color, unlit by the scene's lights.
- `billboard`: Keep the entity turned to face the camera.
- `pooled`: Reuse a pooled slot for this entity.
- `radius` *(with `type: "light"`)*: How far a `light` reaches, in world units (default `30`).
- `coneAngle` *(with `type: "light"`)*: Half-angle of a `light`'s cone. `0`, the default, leaves it a point light shining every way.
- `dirX` *(with `type: "light"` + `coneAngle`)*: X of the direction a `light`'s cone points (default `0`). Read only when `coneAngle` is set.
- `dirY` *(with `type: "light"` + `coneAngle`)*: Y of the direction a `light`'s cone points (default `0`). Read only when `coneAngle` is set.
- `dirZ` *(with `type: "light"` + `coneAngle`)*: Z of the direction a `light`'s cone points (default `-1`). Read only when `coneAngle` is set.
- `lineWidth` *(with `type: "line"`)*: Line width in pixels, read for the `line` and `line-strip` shapes.
- `lineWidth` *(with `type: "line-strip"`)*: Line width in pixels, read for the `line` and `line-strip` shapes.

entity-remove.markdownDescription:
Removes an entity from the store by id. Pass `pooled: true` to release back to the pool instead.

**Properties:**
- `pooled`: Release to pool instead of removing (default `false`).

entity-move.markdownDescription:
Updates `x`, `y`, and/or `angle` on an entity. Cheaper than `entity-update` for transform-only changes.

**Properties:**
- `x`: New X position.
- `y`: New Y position.
- `angle`: New rotation angle in radians.

entity-update.markdownDescription:
Updates writable fields on an existing entity, by the id in `entity-update`. Every field `entity-add` takes (except `type` and `pooled`, both fixed once a slot is allocated), plus `text` and the `trigger` / `ccd` collision flags.
A no-op when no entity has that id.

**Properties:**
- `group`: Collision group name (default `"default"`).
- `mask`: Collision groups this entity is tested against (default `["default"]`).
- `mesh`: Id of a mesh registered in the store. Under `entity-add: "mesh"` its bounds also become the entity's scale, so the collision AABB matches the geometry; on any other shape the mesh is render-only.
- `vertices`: Flat vertex list, for the `line`, `line-strip` and `points` types.
- `parent`: Id of a parent entity: this entity's transform becomes relative to it. Pass an empty value to detach.
- `translation`: Position `[x, y, z]` (default `[0, 0, 0]`). This is the position field; there is no `x`/`y`.
- `scale`: Size `[sx, sy, sz]` (default `[1, 1, 1]`). This is the size field; there is no `w`/`h`.
- `rotation`: Rotation quaternion `[qx, qy, qz, qw]` (default `[0, 0, 0, 1]`).
- `angle`: Z-axis rotation in degrees, converted to `rotation` for you.
- `rx`: X-axis rotation in degrees, converted to `rotation` for you.
- `ry`: Y-axis rotation in degrees, converted to `rotation` for you.
- `rotation-velocity`: Derive `rotation` from a velocity vector `[x, y, z]`, so the entity faces the way it travels.
- `vx`: Velocity along X.
- `vy`: Velocity along Y.
- `vz`: Velocity along Z.
- `ax`: Constant acceleration along X, added to gravity each step.
- `ay`: Constant acceleration along Y, added to gravity each step.
- `az`: Constant acceleration along Z, added to gravity each step.
- `mass`: Body mass (default `1`). `0` makes it infinitely heavy, so collisions never move it.
- `restitution`: Bounciness from 0 (dead stop) to 1 (no energy lost).
- `friction`: Surface friction applied on contact.
- `damping`: Per-entity velocity damping from 0 to 1, overriding the world's `damping`.
- `moveX`: Pin the X velocity each step, after gravity and damping, for driven (character-style) movement. Pass `null` to hand the axis back to the simulation.
- `moveY`: Pin the Y velocity each step, after gravity and damping, for driven (character-style) movement. Pass `null` to hand the axis back to the simulation.
- `physics`: Simulate this entity. Without it the entity is drawn but never stepped.
- `fixed`: Immovable body: it collides but is never moved by a collision.
- `visible`: Draw this entity (default `true`). Hiding one hides its children too.
- `color`: RGBA `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1 (default `[1, 1, 1, 1]`).
- `uv`: Texture sub-rect `[u, v, w, h]`, for drawing one frame out of an atlas.
- `opacity`: Opacity from 0 to 1.
- `texture`: Name of a texture loaded with `gl-texture`.
- `normalMap`: Name of a texture to light the surface with as a normal map.
- `normalScale`: How strongly `normalMap` perturbs the surface.
- `lineWidth`: Line width in pixels, read for the `line` and `line-strip` shapes.
- `borderRadius`: Corner radius in pixels, rounding the box an entity with depth (`scale[2]` above 0) is drawn as. It replaces the shape's geometry outright, so it is for a quad.
- `shader`: Name of a custom shader registered with `gl-shader`.
- `blend`: Blend mode (default `"normal"`).
- `emissive`: Draw at full color, unlit by the scene's lights.
- `billboard`: Keep the entity turned to face the camera.
- `radius`: How far a `light` reaches, in world units (default `30`).
- `coneAngle`: Half-angle of a `light`'s cone. `0`, the default, leaves it a point light shining every way.
- `dirX`: X of the direction a `light`'s cone points (default `0`). Read only when `coneAngle` is set.
- `dirY`: Y of the direction a `light`'s cone points (default `0`). Read only when `coneAngle` is set.
- `dirZ`: Z of the direction a `light`'s cone points (default `-1`). Read only when `coneAngle` is set.
- `text`: Text to draw on the entity: `{ content, font, fill }`, or a bare string for the defaults (`16px sans-serif`, white).
- `trigger`: Report collisions without resolving them, so the entity is a sensor rather than a solid.
- `ccd`: Continuous collision detection, for a body fast enough to tunnel through a wall in one step.

entity-clear.markdownDescription: Removes all entities from the active store and triggers a re-render.

entity-list.markdownDescription:
Returns all entities in the active store as an array of plain objects.
Pass a group name to filter, or `true` to return all groups.

entity-nearest.markdownDescription:
Returns the entity in `group` closest to the given `x`, `y` point, with an added `distance` field.

**Properties:**
- `x`: Reference X coordinate.
- `y`: Reference Y coordinate.

entity-get.markdownDescription:
Gets a single property or the full object for an entity. Pass `id` as the value and `prop` for a single field.
Omit `prop` to get the full entity object. Supports all data fields plus `worldX`, `worldY`, `worldZ`.

**Properties:**
- `prop`: Property name to get (omit to return the full entity object).

parseGLB.markdownDescription:
Parses a binary GLB buffer. Returns a `Scene` descriptor with deduped meshes
and a flat node list. Pass `name` for stable, human-readable mesh ids.

**Properties:**
- `name`: Optional id prefix (default random).

parseGLTF.markdownDescription:
Parses pre-loaded glTF JSON + sibling buffers. Pass `buffers` as an array
(matching `gltf.buffers[i]` order) or an object keyed by URI.

**Properties:**
- `name`: Optional id prefix (default random).

register-mesh.markdownDescription:
Registers a parsed mesh in the active EntityStore's `meshes` map. Idempotent:
re-registering the same id is a no-op. GL extends this via `gl-register-mesh`,
which additionally uploads the geometry to the GPU.

**Properties:**
- `bounds`: AABB bounds object { min, max }.
- `positions`: Float32Array of XYZ vertex positions.
- `normals`: Float32Array of per-vertex normals (optional).
- `uvs`: Float32Array of per-vertex UVs (optional).
- `indices`: Uint16Array / Uint32Array of triangle indices (optional).
- `material`: Material URI map (optional).

collision-on.markdownDescription:
Registers a collision handler that runs `do` steps when entities from two groups collide.
`$collisionA`, `$collisionB`, `$collisionNx/Ny/Nz` are set in context during the steps.

**Properties:**
- `groups`: Two-element array of group names: `[groupA, groupB]`.
- `id`: Optional handler ID (auto-generated if omitted).
- `do` *(required)*: Steps to run on collision. An array runs as a sequence; a single expression is run on its own.
- `thread`: Where `do` runs when physics is threaded. `physics` (default) runs it in the physics worker; use `main` when the steps mutate client/server context, DOM, or network state the owning thread reads.

collision-off.markdownDescription: Removes a collision handler by the `id` that `collision-on` registered it under. Unknown ids are a no-op.

joint-add.markdownDescription:
Create a constraint between two entities.

**Properties:**
- `type`: Constraint type (default `"distance"`).
  - `distance`: Holds the two anchors at `restLength` apart.
  - `spring`: Pulls the anchors toward `restLength` with a damped spring force.
  - `hinge`: Pins the two anchors together, optionally limiting the relative angle.
- `a`: ID of first entity.
- `b`: ID of second entity.
- `anchorA`: Attachment point on A as an `[x, y]` offset from its position (default `[0, 0]`).
- `anchorB`: Attachment point on B as an `[x, y]` offset from its position (default `[0, 0]`).
- `restLength` *(with `type: "distance"`)*: Rest length (default: current distance between entities).
- `restLength` *(with `type: "spring"`)*: Rest length (default: current distance between entities).
- `stiffness` *(with `type: "spring"`)*: Constraint stiffness 0–1 (default `0.5`).
- `damping` *(with `type: "spring"`)*: Constraint damping 0–1 (default `0.1`).
- `minAngle` *(with `type: "hinge"`)*: Lower limit of B's angle relative to A, in degrees. Enforced only when `maxAngle` is set too.
- `maxAngle` *(with `type: "hinge"`)*: Upper limit of B's angle relative to A, in degrees. Enforced only when `minAngle` is set too.

physics-init.markdownDescription:
Initializes the physics simulation loop for the active entity store.
Must be called after `entity-init`. Restarts any existing loop.

**Properties:**
- `gravity`: Gravity vector `[gx, gy]` or `[gx, gy, gz]` (default `[0, 980]`).
- `damping`: Linear velocity damping factor 0–1 (default `0.01`).
- `bounds`: World boundary object `{x, y, w, h}` or `"canvas"`, or `null` for unbounded.
- `start`: Auto-start the simulation loop (default `true`). Set `false` to create the world without a loop and drive it yourself with `physics-step` (e.g. a server authoritative tick), which avoids double-stepping.
- `hz`: Loop tick rate in Hz (e.g. `30`). The loop fires at this fixed rate via a timer instead of RAF (client) / the default ~60Hz timer (server). Physics still steps at the fixed timestep internally; this only sets how often the loop runs, e.g. for a server authoritative tick.

physics-step.markdownDescription:
Run a single physics step without managing a loop.
For use inside a tick loop for server-side authoritative simulation.

**Properties:**
- `dt`: Delta time in seconds (default `1/60`).

physics-pause.markdownDescription: Pauses the world's simulation loop, leaving every entity where it is. Resume with `physics-resume`.

physics-resume.markdownDescription: Resumes a world paused by `physics-pause`. The elapsed-time accumulator is reset, so the pause does not replay as one huge step.

physics-destroy.markdownDescription: Tears the world down: stops the loop, shuts down the physics worker when threaded, and drops the world. A no-op when no world exists.

physics-apply.markdownDescription:
Applies an impulse to one entity by id, changing its velocity immediately. A no-op when the entity is not in the world.

**Properties:**
- `impulse`: Impulse vector `[x, y, z]`. Omit `z` for 2D worlds.

physics-raycast.markdownDescription:
Casts a ray through the world and returns every entity it hits, nearest first. Works on both client and server.

**Properties:**
- `from` *(required)*: Ray origin `{ x, y, z }`. `z` defaults to 0.
- `dir` *(required)*: Ray direction `{ x, y, z }`. `z` defaults to 0.
- `mask`: Only hit entities in these collision groups. Omit to hit every entity.

**Returns:** An array of hits ordered by distance, empty when nothing is hit or no world exists.

v-distance.markdownDescription: Returns the Euclidean distance between two vectors. Pass `[a, b]`.

v-lerp.markdownDescription: Linearly interpolates between two vectors. Pass `[a, b, t]` where `t` is 0–1.

prefixItems.description: The starting vector `a` (`{ x, y, z? }`).
The target vector `b` (`{ x, y, z? }`).

v-toward.markdownDescription: Moves vector `a` toward `b` by at most `maxDist`. Returns `b` if already within range. Pass `[a, b, maxDist]`.

v-normalize.markdownDescription: Returns the unit vector (length 1) in the same direction. Works in 2D and 3D.

prefixItems.description: The vector to scale (`{ x, y, z? }`).

v-scale.markdownDescription: Multiplies a vector by a scalar. Pass `[vector, scalar]`. Works in 2D and 3D.

v-add.markdownDescription: Adds two vectors component-wise. Pass `[a, b]`. Works in 2D and 3D.

prefixItems.description: The minuend vector `a` (`{ x, y, z? }`).
The subtrahend vector `b` (`{ x, y, z? }`).

v-sub.markdownDescription: Subtracts vector `b` from `a`. Pass `[a, b]`. Works in 2D and 3D.

v-direction.markdownDescription: Returns the unit vector from `a` pointing toward `b`. Pass `[from, to]`.

v-cross.markdownDescription: Returns the cross product of two vectors as a 3D vector. Pass `[a, b]`.

v-dot.markdownDescription: Returns the scalar dot product of two vectors. Pass `[a, b]`. Works in 2D and 3D.

cache-connect.markdownDescription:
Initializes the cache singleton. The value selects the driver; connection details vary by driver. Redis also accepts a `url` connection string in place of the discrete host/port properties — memcached does not, because its connection format is the server list itself.

**Operations** *(value of `cache-connect`)*:
- `redis` → string: Redis driver.
- `memcached` → string: Memcached driver. There is no `url` here as there is for `redis`: memcached's connection format is the `host:port` server list itself, with credentials alongside, which is what providers hand you. TLS is not supported by the underlying `memjs` client — tunnel it (stunnel, a service mesh) or use Redis where the traffic must be encrypted.
- `memory` → string: In-memory driver.

**Properties:**
- `prefix`: Key prefix applied to every operation.
- `defaultTtl`: Default TTL in seconds when `ttl` is omitted on set.
- `tls` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"`)*: TLS for the connection, also spelled `ssl`. `true` encrypts AND verifies against the system trust store — the strictest setting, which fails on a private CA. An object takes `ca`, `cert`, `key`, `passphrase`, `servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `minVersion` and `ciphers`. The string forms (`"true"`, `"1"`, `"require"`, `"false"`, `"0"`, `"disable"`) are for a value arriving from `$env` as text. Implied by a `rediss://` url.

Certificates are PEM **content**, not paths: load the file first with `{ "file": "/certs/redis-ca.pem", "raw": true, "as": "ca" }` and pass `{ "var": "$ca" }`.
- `url` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"`)*: Connection string, e.g. `rediss://user:pass@host:6379/0`. `redis://` is plaintext, `rediss://` negotiates TLS. Carries host, port, credentials and database index, so it replaces `host`.
- `host` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"`)*: Redis hostname, spelling the endpoint out instead of passing a `url`.
- `port` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"` + `host`)*: Redis port (default 6379).
- `username` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"` + `host`)*: ACL username (Redis 6+).
- `password` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"` + `host`)*: Auth password.
- `db` *(with `cache-connect: "redis"` + `host`)*: Database index.
- `servers` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"`)*: Server list as `host:port` strings.
- `host` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"`)*: Hostname of a single server, the shorthand for a one-entry `servers`.
- `username` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"` + `servers`)*: SASL username.
- `password` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"` + `servers`)*: SASL password.
- `port` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"` + `host`)*: Port (default 11211).
- `username` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"` + `host`)*: SASL username.
- `password` *(with `cache-connect: "memcached"` + `host`)*: SASL password.
- `maxSize` *(with `cache-connect: "memory"`)*: Maximum entry count.
- `checkPeriod` *(with `cache-connect: "memory"`)*: Expiry sweep interval in seconds.

**Returns:** The connected driver name (`"memory"`, `"redis"`, or `"memcached"`).

cache-get.markdownDescription:
Reads the value stored under `key`.

**Returns:** The stored value (any JSON type), or `null` if the key is absent or expired.

cache-set.markdownDescription:
Writes the `value` sibling under the given key. Optional `ttl` sibling sets expiry in seconds.

**Properties:**
- `value`: Value to store.
- `ttl`: Time-to-live in seconds.

**Returns:** The driver's write result, resolved once the value is stored (truthy on success).

cache-delete.markdownDescription:
Removes the entry under `key`.

**Returns:** `true` if the key existed and was removed, otherwise `false`.

cache-has.markdownDescription:
Checks whether `key` is present in the cache.

**Returns:** `true` if the key is present (and unexpired), otherwise `false`.

cache.markdownDescription:
Cache lifecycle / bulk operation (the value is the op).

**Operations** *(value of `cache`)*:
- `close` → null: Closes the cache connection.
- `clear` → null: Removes every entry.
- `stats` → object: Reports driver statistics.
- `dump` → object: Snapshots the cache contents (memory driver only).

sha256.markdownDescription:
Computes the SHA-256 digest of a string. Pass `encoding` for `base64` or `base64url` instead of hex, which is what a digest going into a header or a URL wants.

**Properties:**
- `encoding`: Digest encoding (default `"hex"`).

**Returns:** A 64-character lowercase hex string, or the digest in the requested `encoding`.

hmac.markdownDescription:
Computes an HMAC of the message under the key. This is what verifies a signed webhook: recompute the signature over the raw body and compare it to the header the sender supplied, with `timingSafeEqual` rather than `eq`.

**Properties:**
- `algorithm`: Hash backing the MAC (default `"sha256"`).
- `encoding`: Output encoding (default `"hex"`).

**Returns:** The MAC in the requested `encoding` (hex by default).

prefixItems.description: One value, e.g. the signature a caller sent.
The other, e.g. the signature you computed.

timingSafeEqual.markdownDescription:
Compares two strings in constant time. Use it for anything secret: an `eq` on a token or a signature returns as soon as the first byte differs, and the time that takes tells an attacker how much of a guess was right.

Both sides are digested before comparing, so values of different lengths compare safely and the comparison leaks no length.

**Returns:** `true` when the two are identical.

encrypt.markdownDescription:
Encrypts a string with AES-256-GCM using the app secret key (`APP_SECRET` env or an auto-generated `app/secret.key`).

**Returns:** A string `"iv:authTag:ciphertext"` (all hex). Pass it back to `decrypt` to recover the plaintext.

decrypt.markdownDescription:
Decrypts a string previously produced by `encrypt` (expects `"iv:authTag:ciphertext"`, all hex).

**Returns:** The original plaintext string. Throws if the format is malformed or the GCM auth tag fails to verify.

hash.markdownDescription:
Hashes a password with bcrypt. Pass `"rounds"` for the cost factor (default 10).

**Properties:**
- `rounds`: Bcrypt cost factor (default `10`).

**Returns:** A bcrypt hash string (e.g. `$2b$10$…`), safe to store. Check it later with `verify`.

prefixItems.description: The stored bcrypt hash to compare against.

verify.markdownDescription:
Compares a plaintext password against a bcrypt hash.

**Returns:** `true` if the password matches the hash, otherwise `false`.

randomHex.markdownDescription:
Generates cryptographically random bytes (default 32).

**Returns:** A hex string `2 × bytes` characters long.

uuid.markdownDescription:
Generates a random (version 4) UUID. Use it for an id a database has not issued yet: an idempotency key, a correlation id, a row id chosen before the insert.

**Returns:** A 36-character UUID, e.g. `"3f8a1c2e-…"`.

database.markdownDescription:
Manages database connections. Supports SQLite (`better-sqlite3`), MySQL (`mysql2`), and PostgreSQL (`pg`) via Knex. The operation is the primary value; each carries its own properties.

**Operations** *(value of `database`)*:
- `connect` → object: Opens (and registers) a connection, from a `url` connection string or from discrete `host`/`port`/`user` properties. Returns a status object.
- `close` → object: Closes a named connection.
- `raw`: Runs a raw SQL string with positional bindings.
- `tableExists` → boolean: Returns whether a table exists.
- `dropTable` → object: Drops a table if it exists. Returns a status object.
- `info` → object: Reports connection info (type, location, whether TLS is on, size, table count).

**Properties:**
- `name` *(with `database: "connect"`)*: Connection name (default `"default"`).
- `ssl` *(with `database: "connect"`)*: TLS for the connection (MySQL / PostgreSQL), also spelled `tls`. `true` encrypts AND verifies against the system trust store — the strictest setting, which fails on the private CAs most managed databases use. `false` forces plaintext, and is the only way to say that: every object turns TLS on. An object takes `ca`, `cert`, `key`, `passphrase`, `servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `minVersion` and `ciphers`. The string forms (`"true"`, `"1"`, `"require"`, `"false"`, `"0"`, `"disable"`) are for a value arriving from `$env` as text.

Certificates are PEM **content**, not paths: load the file first with `{ "file": "/certs/ca.pem", "raw": true, "as": "ca" }` and pass `{ "var": "$ca" }`, so one node owns file reading and one set of path rules applies. (A url's `sslrootcert=` stays a path — that is what the standard defines it as.)

Says HOW to connect rather than where, so it applies to `url` and `host` alike, merging key-wise over whatever the url's `sslmode` implied.
- `url` *(with `database: "connect"`)*: Connection string, e.g. `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/app?sslmode=verify-full`, `mysql://user:pass@host/app?ssl-mode=VERIFY_CA`, or `sqlite:./data.db`. The scheme selects the driver. TLS query parameters are accepted in both standard spellings — libpq's `sslmode`, `sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `sslpassword` and MySQL's `ssl-mode`, `ssl-ca`, `ssl-cert`, `ssl-key`, `ssl-cipher` — and apply to either driver. Following node-postgres rather than the libpq spec, every mode except `disable`/`DISABLED` verifies the server certificate; use `no-verify` to encrypt without verifying. Carries the whole endpoint, so it replaces `host` and `filename`.
- `host` *(with `database: "connect"`)*: Server hostname, spelling the endpoint out instead of passing a `url` (MySQL / PostgreSQL).
- `filename` *(with `database: "connect"`)*: SQLite file path, spelling the endpoint out instead of passing a `url`. It names the driver on its own, so no `type` is needed alongside it.
- `type` *(required)* *(with `database: "connect"` + `host`)*: Database driver.
- `port` *(with `database: "connect"` + `host`)*: Server port (default 3306 for MySQL, 5432 for PostgreSQL).
- `user` *(with `database: "connect"` + `host`)*: Username.
- `password` *(with `database: "connect"` + `host`)*: Password.
- `db` *(with `database: "connect"` + `host`)*: Database name.
- `name` *(with `database: "close"`)*: Connection name to close.
- `sql` *(with `database: "raw"`)*: Raw SQL string.
- `bindings` *(with `database: "raw"`)*: Positional bindings for the SQL.
- `connection` *(with `database: "raw"`)*: Named connection (default if omitted).
- `table` *(with `database: "tableExists"`)*: Table name.
- `connection` *(with `database: "tableExists"`)*: Named connection (default if omitted).
- `table` *(with `database: "dropTable"`)*: Table name.
- `connection` *(with `database: "dropTable"`)*: Named connection (default if omitted).
- `name` *(with `database: "info"`)*: Connection name.

defer.markdownDescription:
Renders a placeholder immediately, then streams the resolved content to replace it via a `<script>` tag.
Use `"loader"` for the placeholder expression shown while the content resolves.
Pass `"delay"` (ms) to add an artificial delay before resolving.

**Properties:**
- `loader`: Placeholder expression shown while the deferred content loads.
- `delay`: Milliseconds to wait before resolving (for staggered loading effects).

**Returns:** A `<div>` wrapper **string** containing the loader, returned right away. The real content resolves in the background and is streamed in to replace it (requires the response to be sent as a streaming HTML response).

email.markdownDescription:
Sends an email via SMTP to one address or a list of them, over the transport `email-connect` opened. Requires `subject`; use `body` for plain text, `html` for an HTML body, or both.

A delivery failure throws a `502` HTTP error, so an enclosing `catch` gets `$error.status` and `$error.message`, plus `$smtp` (`{ code, responseCode, command }`) telling apart an auth rejection from a refused connection. A send where every recipient was rejected throws the same way, so nothing is reported as sent that was not.

**Properties:**
- `subject` *(required)*: Subject line. Required: a send without one is treated as a mistake rather than sent unlabelled.
- `body`: Plain text body. Can be sent alongside `html`, which is what mail clients prefer.
- `html`: HTML body.
- `from`: Sender address, overriding the `from` set on `email-connect`.
- `cc`: Carbon copy: one address or a list.

How many recipients a message may carry across `to`, `cc` and `bcc` is the server's policy, not this node's: RFC 5321 guarantees only 100, and providers range from 50 (SES, Postmark) to 1000 (SendGrid). Past the cap the server answers `452` and the send throws, so a larger audience wants sending in batches.
- `bcc`: Blind carbon copy: one address or a list, hidden from the other recipients.
- `replyTo`: Where replies should go, when that is not the sender.
- `priority`: Message importance, written as the `X-Priority`, `X-MSMail-Priority` and `Importance` headers that clients read. `"normal"` is the default and writes nothing at all, so it is only worth passing to override a value coming from an expression.

It marks the message, it does not speed it up: the server queues it the same either way, and a `"high"` on routine mail is the kind of thing spam filters notice.
- `inReplyTo`: The message id this one answers, which is what makes a client file it under the existing conversation instead of starting a new one. It is the `messageId` a previous `email` step returned, so a ticket or comment thread stores that and passes it back here.
- `references`: Every message id already in the thread, oldest first, with the one in `inReplyTo` last. Most clients thread on this rather than on `inReplyTo` alone, so a long conversation needs the chain, not just the parent.
- `list`: The `List-*` headers, keyed by the part after the dash. A value is a url, or `{ "url": …, "comment": … }` to label it, or a list of either.

Nodemailer writes the angle brackets and formatting, which is the reason to spell them here rather than as raw `headers`. One caveat for bulk mail: the one-click header Gmail and Yahoo require is `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, which is not part of this set, so it still goes in `headers` alongside.
- `icalEvent`: A calendar invitation, which is what makes a client render an accept/decline card instead of a dead attachment. Either the calendar text itself, or `{ method, content, filename }`.

`method` must match the `METHOD:` inside the content: `REQUEST` to invite, `CANCEL` to withdraw, `PUBLISH` (the default) for an event that is merely announced. Content is text or bytes, never a path, so load an `.ics` with `file` first.
- `attachments`: Files to attach, each `{ filename, content }`. Content is bytes or text, never a path. Load it the way Jexs loads anything, `{ "file": "/reports/x.pdf", "as": "pdf" }`, then pass `{ "var": "$pdf" }`.
- `headers`: Extra message headers, each value resolved as an expression. For the ones mail infrastructure reads rather than people:

- **Deliverability.** `List-Unsubscribe` with `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`, which Gmail and Yahoo have required from bulk senders since February 2024. `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated` keeps out-of-office bots from replying to a password reset.
- **Provider instructions.** `X-SMTPAPI` (SendGrid), `X-Mailgun-Variables`, `X-PM-Metadata-*` (Postmark), `X-SES-MESSAGE-TAGS`, which carry tags and metadata that come back on the provider's delivery webhooks.
- **Your own.** A correlation id tying the send back to the request that caused it.

Not for anything with its own sibling or nodemailer option (`replyTo`, message id, date, priority, the `List-*` set), which this would only fight.

**Returns:** `{ messageId, accepted, rejected, response }`. `accepted` and `rejected` are address lists, so a send that reached some recipients but not all is visible rather than silent. Adds `previewUrl` on the Ethereal development transport.

email-connect.markdownDescription:
Opens the SMTP transport every `email` step then sends over. The value is a connection string (`smtps://user:pass@smtp.example.com`), a bare hostname with the details in siblings, or `"ethereal"` for a development transport that captures mail and returns a preview URL instead of delivering it.

Call it once at startup, reading credentials the way any other value arrives, `{ "var": "$env.SMTP_URL" }`. A later call replaces the transport. There is no implicit configuration: without this, an `email` step says so rather than guessing.

**Properties:**
- `port`: Port (default `465` when `secure`, otherwise `587`).
- `user`: Username for SMTP auth. Omit both this and `password` for a relay that takes none.
- `password`: Password for SMTP auth.
- `from`: Default sender for every message that does not give its own `from`.
- `secure`: **When** TLS starts, as opposed to `tls`, which is whether it is used at all. `true` encrypts from the first byte, the port-465 style; `false` starts in plaintext and upgrades with STARTTLS, the port-587 style. Defaults from the port (465) or the url scheme (`smtps://`), so it is only worth setting for a provider doing implicit TLS on some other port.
- `tls`: TLS for the connection, also spelled `ssl`, and the same knob it is on `cache-connect` and `database`. `true` encrypts and verifies against the system trust store, and **fails** rather than sending in the clear. Worth setting on any connection that is not already `secure`, because SMTP's own default is to upgrade only if the server offers to, which is exactly what an attacker strips. An object does the same with its own material: `ca`, `cert`, `key`, `passphrase`, `servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `minVersion`, `ciphers`. `false` refuses TLS altogether, for a local relay that has none.

Certificates are PEM **content**, not paths: load the file first with `{ "file": "/certs/smtp-ca.pem", "raw": true, "as": "ca" }` and pass `{ "var": "$ca" }`.
- `timeout`: Milliseconds to wait for the connection, the greeting, and each socket read. Unset leaves nodemailer's own two-minute defaults.

**Returns:** The configured host.

file.markdownDescription:
Loads a JSON file and resolves it as a Jexs expression. Paths resolve like a filesystem: relative to the file doing the loading (`"nav.json"`, `"../shared/x.json"`), while a leading `/` anchors at the resolver root (`"/data/site.json"`).
Arrays are executed as step sequences; objects are resolved as a single expression.
Pass `"data": true` to skip resolution and get the raw parsed JSON (use for data files, route trees, and anywhere you want the resolver to leave the file alone).
Pass `"raw": true` for the raw string content with no JSON parse.
Pass `"params"` to merge scoped variables into the file's resolution context, or `"write"` to write data to the file.

**Properties:**
- `raw`: Return raw string content without parsing.
- `data`: Parse JSON but skip expression resolution.
- `params`: Scoped variables passed into the loaded file's context.
- `write` → boolean: Writes data to the file (strings verbatim, otherwise JSON). Returns `true`/`false` for success.
- `exists` → boolean: Reports whether the path exists, without reading it. Cheaper than loading a large file to test for it, and unlike a load it does not treat an unparseable file as missing.
- `stat` → object: Reports file metadata without reading the contents.
- `delete` → boolean: Deletes the file. Already absent counts as success, so cleanup steps are repeatable. Refuses directories, since there is deliberately no recursive delete.
- `copyTo` → boolean: Copies the file to another path, overwriting any file already there. The destination resolves the same way the source does.
Named `copyTo` rather than `copy` because `copy` is the client's clipboard op, and a step carrying both keys would dispatch on whichever came first.
- `moveTo` → boolean: Moves or renames the file, overwriting any file already there. The destination resolves the same way the source does.
Falls back to copy-then-delete when the destination is on another drive or mount, which a plain rename cannot cross.

**Returns:** Default: the file resolved as a Jexs expression (a JSON array runs as steps → its last value; a JSON object resolves to its value). With `data: true`, the raw parsed JSON; with `raw: true`, the file as a string; non-JSON text files return their string and binaries a Buffer. `null` if the file can't be read or parsed.

directory.markdownDescription:
Lists directory contents. The path resolves relative to the file doing the loading; a leading `/` anchors at the resolver root. Lists files by default; pass `"subdirectories": true` to list the folders instead.

**Properties:**
- `recursive`: Traverse subdirectories recursively.
- `extension`: Filter by file extension(s), e.g. `"json"`.
- `subdirectories`: List subdirectories instead of files. Combine with `recursive` to walk the whole folder tree.
- `create` → boolean: Creates the directory, auto-creating any missing parent directories (no error if it already exists). Returns `true`/`false` for success.

**Returns:** An array of `{ name, path, size, modified }` entries: files by default, or subdirectories when `subdirectories` is set (filtered by `extension` when given); `[]` if the directory can't be read.

disk.markdownDescription:
Reports disk usage for a path. Pass a path string or `true` to use the current working directory.

**Returns:** `{ total, free, used }` in bytes, or `null` on error.

oauth.markdownDescription:
OAuth 2.0 flow helpers. The operation is the primary value.
Built-in providers: `google`, `github`, `facebook`, `discord`, `twitter`, `microsoft`.

**Operations** *(value of `oauth`)*:
- `configure` → object: Registers provider credentials. Returns a status object.
- `authUrl` → string: Builds the provider authorization URL.
- `exchange` → object: Exchanges an authorization `code` for tokens.
- `refresh` → object: Refreshes tokens using a `refreshToken`.
- `userInfo` → object: Fetches the user profile for a bearer `accessToken`.
- `state` → string: Returns a random CSRF state string.
- `providers` → array: Returns the array of configured provider names.

**Properties:**
- `provider` *(with `oauth: "configure"`)*: Provider name (`"google"`, `"github"`, `"facebook"`, `"discord"`, `"twitter"`, `"microsoft"`).
- `clientId` *(with `oauth: "configure"`)*: OAuth client ID.
- `clientSecret` *(with `oauth: "configure"`)*: OAuth client secret.
- `provider` *(with `oauth: "authUrl"`)*: Provider name (`"google"`, `"github"`, `"facebook"`, `"discord"`, `"twitter"`, `"microsoft"`).
- `redirectUri` *(with `oauth: "authUrl"`)*: OAuth redirect URI.
- `provider` *(with `oauth: "exchange"`)*: Provider name (`"google"`, `"github"`, `"facebook"`, `"discord"`, `"twitter"`, `"microsoft"`).
- `code` *(with `oauth: "exchange"`)*: Authorization code from redirect.
- `redirectUri` *(with `oauth: "exchange"`)*: OAuth redirect URI.
- `provider` *(with `oauth: "refresh"`)*: Provider name (`"google"`, `"github"`, `"facebook"`, `"discord"`, `"twitter"`, `"microsoft"`).
- `refreshToken` *(with `oauth: "refresh"`)*: Refresh token.
- `provider` *(with `oauth: "userInfo"`)*: Provider name (`"google"`, `"github"`, `"facebook"`, `"discord"`, `"twitter"`, `"microsoft"`).
- `accessToken` *(with `oauth: "userInfo"`)*: Bearer token.

webpush.markdownDescription:
Sends a Web Push notification to a browser subscription using VAPID.
Requires `"subject"` (a `mailto:` URL), `"publicKey"`, `"privateKey"`, `"to"` (PushSubscription object), and `"title"`.
Optional: `"body"`, `"icon"`, `"badge"`, `"data"`, `"ttl"`, `"urgency"`, `"topic"`.

**Properties:**
- `subject`: VAPID subject as a `mailto:` URL (e.g. `"mailto:admin@app.com"`).
- `publicKey`: VAPID public key.
- `privateKey`: VAPID private key.
- `to`: PushSubscription object from the browser.
- `title`: Notification title.
- `body`: Notification body text.
- `icon`: Notification icon URL.
- `ttl`: Time-to-live in seconds.
- `urgency`: Push urgency level.
- `topic`: Topic tag to replace earlier notifications with the same topic.

**Returns:** A delivery result object (e.g. `{ statusCode }`) from the push service. Errors if the subscription is invalid or expired (status 404/410), so handle it with `catch` to prune dead subscriptions.

query.markdownDescription:
Runs a database query. The value is the SQL operation; `table` is the target and `options` holds the op-specific clauses.

**Operations** *(value of `query`)*:
- `select` → any: Reads rows. Returns an array (or the single row / `null` with `first`).
- `insert` → any: Inserts `data` (object or array of rows). Returns the PK(s), or the rows with `returning`.
- `upsert` → any: Inserts or updates on `conflict`. `merge` limits which columns update.
- `update` → number: Updates matching rows. `increment`/`decrement` apply atomic deltas. Returns the row count (or rows with `returning`).
- `delete` → number: Deletes matching rows (requires `where`). Returns the row count (or rows with `returning`).
- `count` → number: Counts matching rows; supports joins and `distinct` + `columns`.
- `create` → array: Creates table(s) from a registered `schema` or inline document. Returns a per-table status array.
- `drop` → object: Drops the table.
- `alter` → object: Alters the table: add columns via `addColumns`.

**Properties:**
- `table`: Target table.
- `connection`: Named DB connection (default if omitted).
- `system`: Skip the schema validator.
- `options` *(with `query: "select"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "insert"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "upsert"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "update"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "delete"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "count"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "create"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "drop"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.
- `options` *(with `query: "alter"`)*: Op-specific query clauses.

routes.markdownDescription:
Matches the incoming request path and method against a route tree, then executes the handler.
Supports exact segments, `*` (single param with optional `paramName`/`paramRegex`),
`**` (catch-all), conditional `"if"` guards per node, and `queryParams`/`body` validation.

A handler is a `file` to render or a `run` of steps, never both, or an expression resolving to one of those. A `WS` handler completes a WebSocket upgrade by calling `socket-accept` as a `run` step.

**Returns:** The matched handler's result. A `file`/`run` step that renders to a string is wrapped as `{ response: <html> }`; a handler that returns an object passes it through unchanged, as either a response envelope (`{ response, responseStatus, responseType, responseHeaders }`) or a bare JSON value. Throws a 404 HTTP error when no route matches, so use a catch-all route (`**`) or wrap calls in `catch` to handle not-found.

schema.markdownDescription:
Registers table schemas for use by QueryNode. The operation is the primary value.

**Operations** *(value of `schema`)*:
- `register` → object: Registers schemas from a directory `path` or an inline `table` document.
- `get` → object: Returns a registered table schema by name.
- `list` → array: Returns all registered table schemas.
- `validator` → null: Sets a global schema validator step sequence.
- `validate` → object: Validates `data` against a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12): either a `document` handed in, or the schema registered for `table`. Returns the result rather than throwing, so the caller decides what a failure means.

**Properties:**
- `path` *(with `schema: "register"`)*: Directory of JSON schema files to load.
- `table` *(with `schema: "register"`)*: A table JSON Schema document to register inline.
- `table` *(with `schema: "get"`)*: Table name to retrieve.
- `run` *(with `schema: "validator"`)*: Step sequence to run as a schema validator.
- `data` *(with `schema: "validate"`)*: The value to check. Pass it through a `var` (loaded with `data: true`) when it is itself a Jexs template, otherwise it resolves as an expression before it can be checked.
- `document` *(with `schema: "validate"`)*: The JSON Schema document to check against. Reusing the same object across calls reuses the compiled validator, so load it once and pass it by `var`.
- `table` *(with `schema: "validate"`)*: Name of a registered table schema to check against, instead of `document`.

listen.markdownDescription:
Starts an HTTP listener on the given port. Pass per-request steps in `"do"`.
Set `"client": true` (or a path string) to auto-serve the `@jexs/client` browser bundle
and inject the script tag into rendered `<head>` elements.
Set `"sw"` to an object to enable service worker registration.

**Multiple ports.** Bind more ports by adding more `{ "listen": ..., "do": [...] }` steps. Each is an independent listener with its own `do` pipeline, `client`, `sw`, and `maxBodySize`.

**Per-request `do` execution.** The steps run in order against a fresh per-request context. The universal `"as"` key is honored (stored into the context for later steps), as is `setVars`. Two stop-signals halt the loop early: a step that resolves to `{ "return": X }` (yields `X`) or to a **response object** (a value with a `response` key).

**Response object.** The final value becomes the HTTP response. A bare string is sent as `text/html`; any other bare value is sent as JSON. For full control return an object:
- `response`: the body (string, or any JSON value for `responseType: "json"`). For `responseType: "redirect"` it is the `Location` URL.
- `responseStatus`: HTTP status code (default `200`).
- `responseType`: `"html"` | `"json"` | `"text"` | `"redirect"` | a literal MIME string (e.g. `"image/png"`). When omitted it is inferred: string → `html`, otherwise `json`.
- `responseHeaders` / `responseHeader`: extra response headers (singular overrides plural on collision).

**Properties:**
- `do`: Per-request steps run for each incoming HTTP request. `"as"` and `setVars` write into the shared request context; a step resolving to `{ response }` or `{ return }` ends the loop.
- `client`: Pass `true` to serve the browser bundle at `/jexs`, or a string path to use a custom route.
- `maxBodySize`: Maximum request body size in bytes.
- `sw`: Service worker config object. Pass `{}` to use the default config.

session.markdownDescription:
Manages request sessions stored in cache. Pass an object to set session values. Read values with `{ "var": "$session.key" }`.
Session ID is stored in a `sid` HTTP-only cookie with a 24-hour TTL.

**Returns:** `load` returns `null`; it populates `$session` for reading. `create`/`regenerate`/`destroy`/setting values return a small status object (`{ type: "session", action, sessionId?, cookie }`). The `sid` cookie is queued onto the response for you; you don't return it yourself.

stdio-listen.markdownDescription:
Starts a newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) listener on stdin. Each line is parsed as JSON, set as `$message` in context, and `on-message` steps are run. `console.log` is redirected to stderr to keep stdout clean for protocol data. Use `stdio-write` inside the steps to send output.

**Properties:**
- `on-message`: Steps run per NDJSON line with `$message` in context.
- `on-close`: Optional steps run when stdin closes.

stdio-write.markdownDescription: Writes a value to stdout followed by a newline. Strings pass through unchanged; everything else is JSON-encoded.

stdio-prompt.markdownDescription: Writes a prompt to stdout and reads one line from stdin, resolving to the entered text (trailing newline stripped). Lines are buffered so piped/redirected input works, and resolves to `""` at end of input (EOF), so a non-interactive run never hangs. For interactive CLIs; mutually exclusive with `stdio-listen`. Call `stdio-close` after the last prompt so the process can exit.

stdio-close.markdownDescription: Closes the interactive stdin reader opened by `stdio-prompt`, releasing stdin so the process can exit. Call once, after the final `stdio-prompt`.

tailwind.markdownDescription:
Extracts Tailwind class names from JSON templates and compiles CSS. The operation is the primary value.

**Operations** *(value of `tailwind`)*:
- `extract` → object: Extracts Tailwind classes from `data` and returns `{ classes }`.
- `add` → object: Registers classes from `data` and/or an explicit `classes` list; returns `{ added, total }`.
- `compile` → object: Compiles the registered classes; returns `{ css, classes }`.
- `build` → object: Registers classes from `data` then builds the stylesheet; returns `{ built, classes }`.
- `clear` → object: Clears the class registry; returns `{ cleared: true }`.
- `classes` → array: Returns the registered class names as an array.

**Properties:**
- `data` *(with `tailwind: "extract"`)*: JSON template to extract classes from.
- `data` *(with `tailwind: "add"`)*: JSON template to extract classes from.
- `classes` *(with `tailwind: "add"`)*: Explicit class names to register.
- `data` *(with `tailwind: "build"`)*: JSON template to extract classes from.
- `content` *(with `tailwind: "build"`)*: Glob pattern for additional content sources.

translate.markdownDescription:
Configures automatic string translation for the current request.
Sets `context._translate` so the resolver auto-translates strings via a DB lookup table.

**Properties:**
- `table`: DB table name for translations (default `"translations"`).

**Returns:** Always `null`. It configures translation as a side-effect (via `context._translate`) for the rest of the request.

socket-accept.markdownDescription:
Completes the WebSocket upgrade for the current request and binds per-connection step arrays. Must be called from an upgrade pipeline (where `_upgrade` is in context, populated by the `listen` node's upgrade handling).

**Properties:**
- `on-connect`: Steps run once after the upgrade completes. `_ws`, `_wsPath`, `wsId` available in context.
- `on-message`: Steps run on each incoming message. `$message` is the parsed JSON payload.
- `on-close`: Steps run once when the connection closes.

socket-send.markdownDescription: Sends a message on the current connection (`_ws` in context). Objects are JSON-encoded.

socket-send-to.markdownDescription:
Sends `data` to the peer identified by the connection ID. Objects are JSON-encoded.

**Properties:**
- `data`: Payload to send to the target peer.

socket-broadcast.markdownDescription:
Broadcasts the payload to all peers. With `room`, sends to room members; without `room`, sends to every connection on the same route path. The sender is excluded.

**Properties:**
- `room`: Restrict broadcast to a named room.

socket-join.markdownDescription: Adds the current connection to the named room.

socket-leave.markdownDescription: Removes the current connection from the named room.

socket-count.markdownDescription:
Counts connections in a room (pass the room name) or on the current route path (pass `true`).

**Returns:** The connection count as a number.

socket-list.markdownDescription:
Lists the connections in the named room.

**Returns:** An array of `{ id, ...meta }` objects, one per connection in the room.

url.markdownDescription: URL of the audio file to fetch and decode. Under Electron a relative url resolves against the `app://` scheme and is served from `dist/browser`, so the audio has to ship there like any other asset.

content.markdownDescription: The encoded audio bytes, when something else already loaded them: an ArrayBuffer, a typed array or a Blob. A `fetch` step returns exactly this for a known audio extension, which is the way to load audio that needs headers, credentials or a timeout.

restart.description: Stop any sounds already playing under this name first, instead of overlapping them.

from.description: CSS selector of the hidden input containing serialized JSON.

fields.description: Array of `data-field` names to populate per row.

to.description: CSS selector of the hidden input to write to.

fields.description: Array of `data-field` names to collect per row.

prefix.description: Only intercept requests whose path starts with this (e.g. `"/assets/*"`; the trailing `*` is optional).

data.description: Arbitrary data attached to the notification.

target.description: CSS selector of the container element.

data.description: Initial data array or expression. If omitted, adopts any array already at the context path.

row.description: JSON row template resolved per tree node.

on-change.description: Steps run on each mutation with `$delta` and `$editorData`.

on-select.description: Steps run on selection change with `$selectedPath` and `$selectedNode`.

path.description: Optional tree path to render partially (child-list path or node path). Omit for a full render.
Optional dot-path of the insertion target (within the tree).

key.description: Key to update on the selected node.

direction.markdownDescription: Reorder the selected node up or down among its siblings.

to.markdownDescription: Relocate a node into the list at this path (any list in the tree). Pair with `index` (position) and `from` (a non-selected source node).

index.description: Insertion index within `to` (default: append to the end).

from.description: Source node path to move (default: the currently selected node).

path.description: Dot-path string to select, or `null` to deselect.
Dot-path of the node to toggle.

urls.description: One server URL, or several: `stun:host:port` or `turn:host:port`.

iceServers.markdownDescription: ICE servers to gather candidates from. Defaults to a public STUN server, which is **not** enough for peers behind a symmetric NAT: those need a TURN entry with credentials.

timeout.description: Default milliseconds a `connect` waits for its peer to open. Defaults to 15000.

trickle.markdownDescription: Whether ICE candidates are signalled as they are found (the default). Set `false` to emit nothing until gathering completes, then one description carrying every candidate inline: slower to connect, but it reduces the exchange to a single payload each way, which is what a human-carried transport needs.

on-signal.markdownDescription: Steps that deliver one signalling payload, with `$rtcSignal` (the payload, opaque) and `$rtcPeerId` (who it is for) in scope. Required: without it an offer has nowhere to go.

on-peer.markdownDescription: Steps run when a peer offers us a connection, **before** anything is answered, with `$rtcPeerId` in scope. Resolve to a falsy value to refuse: nothing is signalled back and the peer is dropped. This is the only point at which refusing is still possible.

on-open.markdownDescription: Steps run when a peer's channels are open and `send` is safe, with `$rtcPeerId` and `$rtcInbound` in scope. Fires for peers arriving from either direction, which makes it the answering side's only way to learn this.

on-message.markdownDescription: Steps run on each incoming message, with `$rtcMessage`, `$rtcPeerId` and `$rtcChannel` (`"data"` or `"fast"`) in scope.

on-close.markdownDescription: Steps run when a peer that had opened goes away, with `$rtcPeerId` in scope. A refused offer or a dial that timed out never opened, and is reported by that step instead.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the channels to open before giving up. Defaults to the `listen` value.

data.description: The signalling payload, exactly as it was emitted.
Data to send. Non-string values are JSON-encoded.

name.description: Names this connection, so other steps can address it and a second `ws-connect` does not replace it.

on-open.description: Steps to run when the connection opens, including after a reconnect.

on-message.markdownDescription: Steps to run on each incoming message, with `$wsMessage` in scope: parsed as JSON when it parses, otherwise the raw value. The node reads nothing out of a message itself, so any protocol on top of the socket, an id handed out on connect included, is yours to read here.

on-close.markdownDescription: Steps to run when the connection closes, with `$wsCode`, `$wsReason` and `$wsClean` in scope. A dropped connection lands here too, before the reconnect.

retry.markdownDescription: Reconnect behavior after a connection that opened is lost. `true` (the default) retries forever with backoff, `false` never retries, and a number caps the attempts. The initial connect is not a retry: it either opens or throws.

protocols.description: Subprotocol names offered during the handshake.

binaryType.description: How binary messages arrive: `"blob"` (the browser default) or `"arraybuffer"`.

name.description: Which connection to send on (default: the unnamed one).
Which connection to close (default: the unnamed one).

code.description: Close code (default `1000`, a normal closure). Application codes are 4000-4999.

reason.description: Human-readable reason, at most 123 bytes once encoded.

name.description: Which connection to report on (default: the unnamed one).

do.description: Template to resolve for each item.

unit.description: Force the display unit instead of auto-selecting the largest fitting one.

numeric.description: `"always"` (default, e.g. "1 day ago") or `"auto"` (uses "yesterday"/"tomorrow" where available).

content.description: Children of the element: a string or mixed array of strings and expressions.

events.description: DOM event handlers, keyed by event name: `{ "click": { "do": [...] } }`.

class.description: Class list: a string, array, or `{ className: bool }` map.

style.description: Inline style: a camel/kebab-case object, or a string.

method.description: HTTP method (default `"GET"`). `GET` and `HEAD` never send a body.

headers.markdownDescription: Request headers. Each value is resolved as an expression and matched case-insensitively, so an explicit `Content-Type` replaces the `application/json` default. Entries resolving to `null`/`undefined` are dropped.

type.markdownDescription: Force how the response body is decoded, instead of inferring it from the URL extension and Content-Type. Use it when the server sends the wrong Content-Type, or when the URL carries no extension.

throw.markdownDescription:
Set `false` and the step never interrupts the sequence: not for a non-2xx status, and not for a request that never completed (a timeout, a refused connection).
