Pair with `full` when you need to distinguish whether nothing arrived or the body was empty.

timeout.markdownDescription: Abort the request after this many milliseconds and throw a `408` HTTP error (or resolve, under `throw: false`). `0` (the default) waits indefinitely.

credentials.description: Whether the browser sends cookies and HTTP auth. Use `"include"` for cross-origin cookie auth. Ignored outside the browser.

mode.description: Browser request mode. Ignored outside the browser.

redirect.markdownDescription: How to treat a 3xx: follow it (default), throw, or with `"manual"` hand it back to you. Outside Node the browser opaque-filters a manual redirect: `status` comes back `0` with no headers, and only the fact that it redirected survives.

cache.description: HTTP cache mode. Ignored outside the browser.

full.markdownDescription: Resolves to the whole response instead of the bare body: for a response header such as an `ETag`, or to tell a `201` from a `200`. Shape only: a non-2xx still throws unless you also pass `throw: false`, which is what reading a `redirect: "manual"` 3xx takes.

then.description: Value to resolve when condition is truthy.

else.description: Value to resolve when condition is falsy.

cases.description: Object mapping string keys to result expressions.

default.description: Value to resolve when no case matches.

do.description: Steps or expression to resolve for each item.

item.description: Variable name to expose the current item (default `"item"`).

key.description: Variable name to expose the current index (default `"index"`).

parallel.description: Resolve all iterations concurrently instead of sequentially.

params.description: Scoped variables merged into a shallow copy of the context for the steps.

clampToRange.description: Clamp the result to `[outMin, outMax]` instead of extrapolating (default `false`). Named to avoid colliding with the `clamp` op.

minimumFractionDigits.description: Minimum digits after the decimal point.

maximumFractionDigits.description: Maximum digits after the decimal point.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale tag for the plural-category selection (default: the runtime locale). Suffixes remain English.

item.description: Variable name for the current value (default `"item"`).

do.description: Template to resolve for each value.

urlSafe.description: Use the URL-safe alphabet and drop the `=` padding.

all.description: Replace all occurrences (default `true`). For `/regex/` patterns the `g` flag controls this unless `all` is set explicitly.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale tag for word/sentence boundaries (default: the runtime locale).

detach.description: Run `do` steps fire-and-forget each tick without waiting for completion.

do.description: Steps to execute on each tick. An array runs as a sequence; a single expression is run on its own.
Steps to execute on each interval. An array runs as a sequence; a single expression is run on its own.

raw.description: Skip resolving values and write them directly.

bubble.description: Also write each value into every enclosing scope (parent contexts), so it survives after the current file/loop/branch returns.

params.description: Object passed to the thread: the ONLY data that crosses, and the worker's context (its keys become `$key`). `ArrayBuffer` values transfer zero-copy (detaching the source). Must be structured-cloneable (no DOM nodes, functions, class instances).

do.description: Steps to run on the thread, resolved against `params` as context.

idle.description: Milliseconds to keep the thread warm after its last step before reaping it (default 10000). `0` reaps immediately; a large value keeps a long-lived thread.

do.description: Steps run in the main process when the event fires. An array runs as a sequence; a single expression is run on its own.

properties.description: What the dialog can select (e.g. openFile, openDirectory, multiSelections).

defaultPath.description: Path and filename the dialog opens with.

buttons.description: Button labels; the result is the pressed button's index.

detail.description: Extra detail text below the message.

window.description: Attach to this window instead of setting the application menu.

icon.description: Path to an image shown alongside.

do.description: Steps run in the main process when the notification is clicked.
Steps run in the main process when the shortcut fires.

tooltip.description: Hover text for the tray icon.

items.description: Right-click menu, using the same item shape as `menu`.

do.description: Steps run in the main process when the icon is clicked.

name.description: Register the window under this name instead of the template basename.

frame.description: Set `false` for a frameless window, so the page can draw its own title bar.

allow.description:
Ops this window's page may ask the main process for. Omit for no restriction.
List ops only — a sibling travels with its op, so `["query"]` already covers `{ "query": "select", "table": "saves" }`. Nested values are checked too, so a denied op cannot hide in a sibling slot.
Your own menu, tray and shortcut handlers are unaffected — they run in main and never cross the IPC channel this limits.

titleBarStyle.description: Native title bar treatment. `hidden` keeps the traffic lights on macOS while freeing the bar for custom chrome.

params.description: Values merged into the steps' scope, resolved in the main process before they cross.

clear.description: Background clear color as `[r, g, b, a]` (default `[0,0,0,1]`).

on-frame.description: Steps to run each animation frame (`$dt`, `$time` available).

src.description: URL of the image to load.

linear.description: Use LINEAR filtering instead of NEAREST (default). Set for smooth/upscaled textures and MSDF atlases.

hdr.description: Decode `src` as a Radiance `.hdr` (RGBE) image and upload a float texture (values may exceed 1.0). Use for an equirectangular environment map referenced by a `skybox` setting.

cols.description: Number of columns in the grid.

rows.description: Number of rows in the grid.

frames.description: Array of frame indices from the atlas.

fps.description: Frames per second for the animation.

stop.description: Pass `true` to stop the current animation.

data.description: 2D array of atlas frame indices (rows × columns).

tileWidth.description: Width of each tile in pixels (default `32`).

tileHeight.description: Height of each tile in pixels (default `32`).

x.description: Column of the tile to change (0-based).

y.description: Row of the tile to change (0-based).

tile.description: Atlas frame index to write. `0` clears the tile.

color.description: Trail color as `[r, g, b, a]`.

mask.description: Group names to test against (default: all groups).

font.description: CSS font string for the canvas path (e.g. `"24px Arial"`). Ignored when `msdf` is set.

fill.description: CSS color string for the text fill.

msdf.description: Name of a registered `gl-font` to render this text via the MSDF path (crisp at any scale, recolorable). When set, `font` is ignored and `size` controls the px size.

size.description: Font size in px for the MSDF path. Default `32`.

atlas.description: Name of a `gl-texture` holding the MSDF atlas PNG.

metrics.description: Parsed BMFont-JSON descriptor (from a file/fetch node), or a JSON string.

shared.description: Back the store with SharedArrayBuffers so the host can step physics on a worker thread (off the main thread). Falls back to a normal store if growable SAB is unsupported. Default `false`.

type.markdownDescription:
Entity shape (default `"quad"`). A shape with depth (`scale[2]` above 0) is drawn solid and flat otherwise, so a `circle` is a disc or a cylinder and a `triangle` a triangle or a cone.
`line`, `line-strip` and `points` take their geometry from `vertices`; `mesh` draws the mesh named by `mesh`, taking its scale from the mesh bounds and colliding against its BVH; `ramp` collides as a slope rather than a box; `light` and `pivot` are never drawn.

pooled.description: Reuse a pooled slot for this entity.
Release to pool instead of removing (default `false`).

text.description: Text to draw on the entity: `{ content, font, fill }`, or a bare string for the defaults (`16px sans-serif`, white).

trigger.description: Report collisions without resolving them, so the entity is a sensor rather than a solid.

ccd.description: Continuous collision detection, for a body fast enough to tunnel through a wall in one step.

prop.description: Property name to get (omit to return the full entity object).

groups.description: Two-element array of group names: `[groupA, groupB]`.

do.description: Steps to run on collision. An array runs as a sequence; a single expression is run on its own.

thread.description: Where `do` runs when physics is threaded. `physics` (default) runs it in the physics worker; use `main` when the steps mutate client/server context, DOM, or network state the owning thread reads.

anchorA.description: Attachment point on A as an `[x, y]` offset from its position (default `[0, 0]`).

anchorB.description: Attachment point on B as an `[x, y]` offset from its position (default `[0, 0]`).

minAngle.description: Lower limit of B's angle relative to A, in degrees. Enforced only when `maxAngle` is set too.

maxAngle.description: Upper limit of B's angle relative to A, in degrees. Enforced only when `minAngle` is set too.

gravity.description: Gravity vector `[gx, gy]` or `[gx, gy, gz]` (default `[0, 980]`).

bounds.description: World boundary object `{x, y, w, h}` or `"canvas"`, or `null` for unbounded.

start.description: Auto-start the simulation loop (default `true`). Set `false` to create the world without a loop and drive it yourself with `physics-step` (e.g. a server authoritative tick), which avoids double-stepping.

hz.description: Loop tick rate in Hz (e.g. `30`). The loop fires at this fixed rate via a timer instead of RAF (client) / the default ~60Hz timer (server). Physics still steps at the fixed timestep internally; this only sets how often the loop runs, e.g. for a server authoritative tick.

impulse.description: Impulse vector `[x, y, z]`. Omit `z` for 2D worlds.

from.description: Ray origin `{ x, y, z }`. `z` defaults to 0.

dir.description: Ray direction `{ x, y, z }`. `z` defaults to 0.

mask.description: Only hit entities in these collision groups. Omit to hit every entity.

prefix.description: Key prefix applied to every operation.

defaultTtl.description: Default TTL in seconds when `ttl` is omitted on set.

url.markdownDescription: Connection string, e.g. `rediss://user:pass@host:6379/0`. `redis://` is plaintext, `rediss://` negotiates TLS. Carries host, port, credentials and database index, so it replaces `host`.

host.markdownDescription: Hostname of a single server, the shorthand for a one-entry `servers`.

tls.markdownDescription:
TLS for the connection, also spelled `ssl`. `true` encrypts AND verifies against the system trust store — the strictest setting, which fails on a private CA. An object takes `ca`, `cert`, `key`, `passphrase`, `servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `minVersion` and `ciphers`. The string forms (`"true"`, `"1"`, `"require"`, `"false"`, `"0"`, `"disable"`) are for a value arriving from `$env` as text. Implied by a `rediss://` url.

Certificates are PEM **content**, not paths: load the file first with `{ "file": "/certs/redis-ca.pem", "raw": true, "as": "ca" }` and pass `{ "var": "$ca" }`.

url.markdownDescription: Connection string, e.g. `postgres://user:pass@host:5432/app?sslmode=verify-full`, `mysql://user:pass@host/app?ssl-mode=VERIFY_CA`, or `sqlite:./data.db`. The scheme selects the driver. TLS query parameters are accepted in both standard spellings — libpq's `sslmode`, `sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `sslpassword` and MySQL's `ssl-mode`, `ssl-ca`, `ssl-cert`, `ssl-key`, `ssl-cipher` — and apply to either driver. Following node-postgres rather than the libpq spec, every mode except `disable`/`DISABLED` verifies the server certificate; use `no-verify` to encrypt without verifying. Carries the whole endpoint, so it replaces `host` and `filename`.

host.markdownDescription: Server hostname, spelling the endpoint out instead of passing a `url` (MySQL / PostgreSQL).

filename.markdownDescription: SQLite file path, spelling the endpoint out instead of passing a `url`. It names the driver on its own, so no `type` is needed alongside it.

ssl.markdownDescription:
TLS for the connection (MySQL / PostgreSQL), also spelled `tls`. `true` encrypts AND verifies against the system trust store — the strictest setting, which fails on the private CAs most managed databases use. `false` forces plaintext, and is the only way to say that: every object turns TLS on. An object takes `ca`, `cert`, `key`, `passphrase`, `servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `minVersion` and `ciphers`. The string forms (`"true"`, `"1"`, `"require"`, `"false"`, `"0"`, `"disable"`) are for a value arriving from `$env` as text.

Certificates are PEM **content**, not paths: load the file first with `{ "file": "/certs/ca.pem", "raw": true, "as": "ca" }` and pass `{ "var": "$ca" }`, so one node owns file reading and one set of path rules applies. (A url's `sslrootcert=` stays a path — that is what the standard defines it as.)

Says HOW to connect rather than where, so it applies to `url` and `host` alike, merging key-wise over whatever the url's `sslmode` implied.

port.description: Server port (default 3306 for MySQL, 5432 for PostgreSQL).

loader.description: Placeholder expression shown while the deferred content loads.

delay.description: Milliseconds to wait before resolving (for staggered loading effects).

subject.description: Subject line. Required: a send without one is treated as a mistake rather than sent unlabelled.

body.description: Plain text body. Can be sent alongside `html`, which is what mail clients prefer.

from.description: Sender address, overriding the `from` set on `email-connect`.

cc.markdownDescription:
Carbon copy: one address or a list.

How many recipients a message may carry across `to`, `cc` and `bcc` is the server's policy, not this node's: RFC 5321 guarantees only 100, and providers range from 50 (SES, Postmark) to 1000 (SendGrid). Past the cap the server answers `452` and the send throws, so a larger audience wants sending in batches.

bcc.description: Blind carbon copy: one address or a list, hidden from the other recipients.

replyTo.description: Where replies should go, when that is not the sender.

priority.markdownDescription:
Message importance, written as the `X-Priority`, `X-MSMail-Priority` and `Importance` headers that clients read. `"normal"` is the default and writes nothing at all, so it is only worth passing to override a value coming from an expression.

It marks the message, it does not speed it up: the server queues it the same either way, and a `"high"` on routine mail is the kind of thing spam filters notice.

inReplyTo.markdownDescription: The message id this one answers, which is what makes a client file it under the existing conversation instead of starting a new one. It is the `messageId` a previous `email` step returned, so a ticket or comment thread stores that and passes it back here.

references.markdownDescription: Every message id already in the thread, oldest first, with the one in `inReplyTo` last. Most clients thread on this rather than on `inReplyTo` alone, so a long conversation needs the chain, not just the parent.

list.markdownDescription:
The `List-*` headers, keyed by the part after the dash. A value is a url, or `{ "url": …, "comment": … }` to label it, or a list of either.

Nodemailer writes the angle brackets and formatting, which is the reason to spell them here rather than as raw `headers`. One caveat for bulk mail: the one-click header Gmail and Yahoo require is `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, which is not part of this set, so it still goes in `headers` alongside.

icalEvent.markdownDescription:
A calendar invitation, which is what makes a client render an accept/decline card instead of a dead attachment. Either the calendar text itself, or `{ method, content, filename }`.

`method` must match the `METHOD:` inside the content: `REQUEST` to invite, `CANCEL` to withdraw, `PUBLISH` (the default) for an event that is merely announced. Content is text or bytes, never a path, so load an `.ics` with `file` first.

content.description: The bytes or text to attach. Load a file with `file` and pass the result.

contentType.description: MIME type; inferred from the filename when omitted.

cid.description: Content ID, to reference the attachment from the HTML body as `cid:<value>`.

attachments.markdownDescription: Files to attach, each `{ filename, content }`. Content is bytes or text, never a path. Load it the way Jexs loads anything, `{ "file": "/reports/x.pdf", "as": "pdf" }`, then pass `{ "var": "$pdf" }`.

headers.markdownDescription:
Extra message headers, each value resolved as an expression. For the ones mail infrastructure reads rather than people:

- **Deliverability.** `List-Unsubscribe` with `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`, which Gmail and Yahoo have required from bulk senders since February 2024. `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated` keeps out-of-office bots from replying to a password reset.
- **Provider instructions.** `X-SMTPAPI` (SendGrid), `X-Mailgun-Variables`, `X-PM-Metadata-*` (Postmark), `X-SES-MESSAGE-TAGS`, which carry tags and metadata that come back on the provider's delivery webhooks.
- **Your own.** A correlation id tying the send back to the request that caused it.

Not for anything with its own sibling or nodemailer option (`replyTo`, message id, date, priority, the `List-*` set), which this would only fight.

user.description: Username for SMTP auth. Omit both this and `password` for a relay that takes none.

from.description: Default sender for every message that does not give its own `from`.

secure.markdownDescription: **When** TLS starts, as opposed to `tls`, which is whether it is used at all. `true` encrypts from the first byte, the port-465 style; `false` starts in plaintext and upgrades with STARTTLS, the port-587 style. Defaults from the port (465) or the url scheme (`smtps://`), so it is only worth setting for a provider doing implicit TLS on some other port.

tls.markdownDescription:
TLS for the connection, also spelled `ssl`, and the same knob it is on `cache-connect` and `database`. `true` encrypts and verifies against the system trust store, and **fails** rather than sending in the clear. Worth setting on any connection that is not already `secure`, because SMTP's own default is to upgrade only if the server offers to, which is exactly what an attacker strips. An object does the same with its own material: `ca`, `cert`, `key`, `passphrase`, `servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `minVersion`, `ciphers`. `false` refuses TLS altogether, for a local relay that has none.

Certificates are PEM **content**, not paths: load the file first with `{ "file": "/certs/smtp-ca.pem", "raw": true, "as": "ca" }` and pass `{ "var": "$ca" }`.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the connection, the greeting, and each socket read. Unset leaves nodemailer's own two-minute defaults.

raw.description: Return raw string content without parsing.

data.description: Parse JSON but skip expression resolution.

params.description: Scoped variables passed into the loaded file's context.

write.markdownDescription: Writes data to the file (strings verbatim, otherwise JSON). Returns `true`/`false` for success.

exists.markdownDescription: Reports whether the path exists, without reading it. Cheaper than loading a large file to test for it, and unlike a load it does not treat an unparseable file as missing.

stat.markdownDescription: Reports file metadata without reading the contents.

delete.markdownDescription: Deletes the file. Already absent counts as success, so cleanup steps are repeatable. Refuses directories, since there is deliberately no recursive delete.

copyTo.markdownDescription:
Copies the file to another path, overwriting any file already there. The destination resolves the same way the source does.
Named `copyTo` rather than `copy` because `copy` is the client's clipboard op, and a step carrying both keys would dispatch on whichever came first.

moveTo.markdownDescription:
Moves or renames the file, overwriting any file already there. The destination resolves the same way the source does.
Falls back to copy-then-delete when the destination is on another drive or mount, which a plain rename cannot cross.

subdirectories.description: List subdirectories instead of files. Combine with `recursive` to walk the whole folder tree.

create.markdownDescription: Creates the directory, auto-creating any missing parent directories (no error if it already exists). Returns `true`/`false` for success.

topic.description: Topic tag to replace earlier notifications with the same topic.

groupBy.description: GROUP BY column name or array of names.

first.description: Return a single row instead of an array.

merge.description: Columns to update on conflict (upsert); omit to merge all.

schema.description: Table schema reference or inline document (create).

path.description: Directory of JSON schema files to load.

table.description: A table JSON Schema document to register inline.

run.description: Step sequence to run as a schema validator.

data.description: The value to check. Pass it through a `var` (loaded with `data: true`) when it is itself a Jexs template, otherwise it resolves as an expression before it can be checked.

document.description: The JSON Schema document to check against. Reusing the same object across calls reuses the compiled validator, so load it once and pass it by `var`.

table.description: Name of a registered table schema to check against, instead of `document`.

do.description: Per-request steps run for each incoming HTTP request. `"as"` and `setVars` write into the shared request context; a step resolving to `{ response }` or `{ return }` ends the loop.

client.description: Pass `true` to serve the browser bundle at `/jexs`, or a string path to use a custom route.

maxBodySize.description: Maximum request body size in bytes.

sw.description: Service worker config object. Pass `{}` to use the default config.

on-message.description: Steps run per NDJSON line with `$message` in context.

on-close.description: Optional steps run when stdin closes.

content.description: Glob pattern for additional content sources.

on-connect.description: Steps run once after the upgrade completes. `_ws`, `_wsPath`, `wsId` available in context.

on-message.description: Steps run on each incoming message. `$message` is the parsed JSON payload.

on-close.description: Steps run once when the connection closes.

data.description: Payload to send to the target peer.

room.description: Restrict broadcast to a named room.
